tips.title: Ruffled scrunchie from scalloped-edge strip
tips.notes:
Facebook logged-in pass batch 4 (2026-09-08): caption and frame observations archived in scrapes/d4b2582f6a/notes.md; key frames in scrapes/d4b2582f6a/frames/.
FB yt-dlp cookies+subs batch 2 (2026-09-08): download OK; left linked — no sewing instructional speech (lyrics/music or unrelated narration). See scrapes/d4b2582f6a/dl/. Visual-only pass from downloaded Facebook video.
tips.how_to:
1. **Prepare the fabric:** Start with a long strip of fabric that has finished/scalloped edges along both long sides.
2. **Hem the short ends:** Fold over the raw edges of the two short ends of the fabric strip and stitch them down to create a hem.
3. **Fold lengthwise:** Fold the fabric strip in half lengthwise, wrong sides together, so the patterned right side is facing out.
4. **Sew the casing:** Measure and sew two parallel lines of stitching down the center of the folded fabric (through both layers). This creates a central casing tube while leaving unstitched ruffles on both the folded side and the scalloped edge side.
5. **Prepare the elastic:** Attach a safety pin to one end of a piece of elastic.
6. **Thread the elastic:** Use the safety pin to thread the elastic through the central stitched casing, gathering the fabric as you pull it through.
7. **Secure the elastic:** Pull both ends of the elastic out of the casing and tie them together securely in a knot.
8. **Close the scrunchie:** Bring the two hemmed short ends of the fabric together and join them to close the loop and finish the scrunchie.

tips.title: French bias binding for clean necklines and armholes
tips.notes: Creator: @tessjeanpatterns. Caption: “My go-to method for flawless necklines and armholes… learn the French binding technique for a clean, polished finish.” Clear sampled overlays: “Cut a strip of bias tape 30mm wide”; “Place the binding right sides together along the neckline”; “Start by finishing one armhole so you have one shoulder seam left open.” Not enough of the full sequence for a reliable how-to. Scrape: scrapes/eee4f64652/ Frame pass 2026-09-08: caption describes French binding for polished necklines/armholes. Overlays sampled ~1–55s confirm 30 mm tape, open shoulder, RST placement, 6 mm/¼ in seam, fold/press, trim, topstitch, repeat other armhole, topstitch shoulder flat.
tips.how_to: Cut a 30 mm-wide strip of bias tape, long enough to go around the neckline and both armholes. Leave one shoulder seam open and start by finishing one armhole. Place the binding right sides together along the neckline/edge. Sew a 6 mm (¼ in) seam, then fold the binding back over the seam allowance and press. Trim excess tape close to the stitching, then topstitch 6 mm (¼ in) from the edge. Repeat the same process for the remaining armhole and topstitch the shoulder seam flat.

tips.title: Classic machine shirring with elastic thread
tips.notes: Creator: @abc_sewing. Scrape: scrapes/3df2ad75c0/
tips.how_to: Mark parallel stitch lines on the fabric. Hand-wind shirring elastic onto an empty bobbin without stretching it tight (wind extras if you have many rows). Use regular thread on top; insert the elastic bobbin. Lower top tension to ~2–2.5 and set stitch length ~3.5. Sew along each marked line, backstitching at the start; the bobbin elastic gathers automatically. At row ends, leave the needle down, pivot a few stitches to the next line, and continue. Steam to remove marks and set the gathers.

tips.how_to: Thread the needle. Place the thread ends behind the needle and pinch them. Wrap the thread near the needle end around the needle from back to front; more wraps make a bigger knot. Hold the wraps on the needle and pull the remaining thread through to form the knot.

tips.title: Boxy makeup bag with French-seam corners (updated method)
tips.notes: Uploader: lauren.lieser19. Beginner-friendlier corner finish vs trimming/boxing alone. Screenshot on-screen measurements.
tips.how_to: Fuse outer fabric to fusible fleece and quilt (mark a guide crease, sew the first line, then use a quilting guide bar for even rows). Install a zipper longer than the bag width: sandwich zipper between lining (face up) and outer (face down), sew with a zipper foot; repeat on the other side, press, and topstitch both sides of the zipper. Make double-fold zipper tabs, stitch them at both zipper ends (folded edge facing in; zipper pull parked). Sew outer RST along the bottom (~¼″); sew lining RST along the bottom leaving a center turning gap. Align outer and lining so bottom seams match the zipper, sew both short ends, trim excess zipper, and cut 2″×2″ squares from all four corners. Turn right-side out through the lining gap and close the gap. Match each cut corner into a straight line (outer + lining stacked) and sew ~¼″. Turn wrong-side out and repeat the same corner seam on the lining side for a French-seam finish that also adds structure. Dimensions are shown on-screen in the video.

Sew the hem all the way around, then pull the garment right-side out through the same opening. Understitch the hem toward the lining in small sections through the opening so the lining stays flat, press, and hand-stitch the side opening closed.

tips.title: Shirt yoke burrito method (enclosed yoke + shoulders)

Pull the body out through the neck opening so yoke and shoulder seams are fully enclosed and clean inside.

tips.title: Boxy pouch pattern calculator + French-seam method (Sar Kirsten)

Sandwich zipper between outer and lining RST (zip RS toward outer); sew full Length with your SA; flip and sew the other zip edge the same way. Turn RS out.

tips.how_to:
1. Insert a long, thin, rigid metal rod into the open end of an inside-out fabric tube.
2. Push until the tip rests firmly against the closed/sewn end.

tips.title: Baby wipe clutch (no zipper) with wipe-dispenser oval
tips.notes: Creator: @mariahs_makes. No zipper by design. Scrape: scrapes/842d299828/
tips.how_to: Cut outer, pocket, and strap pieces (mix print + solid); fuse interfacing to all print pieces. Strap: RST, sew ¼″ leaving bottom open, clip curves, turn, press, topstitch ~⅛″. Small pocket + one large pocket: RST sew top at ½″, flip RS out, press, topstitch. Wipe window: two large pocket pieces, fold ½″ at top edges; find center; mark oval (~4″ × 2¾″ or trace your wipe lid); sew oval, cut inside ~¼″ from stitching, clip curves; turn one layer through the oval, press, topstitch oval, then edge-stitch the folded top. Stack: large pocket without window RS up + small pocket centered on bottom (sew center divider if wanted) + wipe-window pocket aligned at top (finished edges toward middle) on outer RS up; stitch ¼″ around. Add strap on non-window side; cover with second outer RST; mark leave-open section; sew ½″; clip curves; turn; press; topstitch. Add snap/Velcro/button with pouch filled to place closure.

tips.title: Boxy makeup pouch with no raw edges (pinch-box corners)
tips.notes: Uploader: jjsimp_. Method keeps corner triangles inside instead of trimming squares.
tips.how_to: Cut two outers, two linings, and two batting pieces ~13″×9″ plus a ~14″ zipper. Quilt outer to batting. Zipper sandwich: outer right-side up, zipper teeth down, lining right-side down; sew; topstitch to keep fabric clear of teeth; repeat on the other zipper side. Sew outer RST and lining RST around the remaining edges, leaving a gap in the lining; clip corners. Unzip partway. Make zipper tabs from a ~2″×7″ strip (fold to a flat tube, stitch edges, cut in half); pin tabs at zipper ends with loop facing inside. Sew the short ends (tabs + zipper), trim excess zipper/tabs. Turn through the lining gap. To box without cutting squares: pinch each corner flat, mark ~2″ from the tip (use a small triangle template if helpful), sew straight across, and leave the triangle flaps inside—no raw cut edges. Close the lining gap. Flip corners out while using for an open tray-like pouch.

tips.title: Double welt inside pocket (no zipper)
tips.notes: Visual-only pass from downloaded Facebook video.
tips.how_to:
1. Place pocket fabric RST on main fabric; draw a horizontal rectangle for the opening (~1″ tall × 4–5″ wide if matching this demo).

tips.title: Boxy zip bag with top handle (bias + boxed corners)
tips.notes: Visual-only pass from downloaded Facebook video.
tips.how_to:
1.  **Prepare the lid:** Take a small quilted fabric rectangle and finish one of the shorter edges with bias tape.
2.  **Attach the zipper:** Sew one side of a zipper face-down along the bound edge. Fold the fabric back and topstitch along the zipper.
3.  **Add the handle:** Pin a fabric strap horizontally across the middle of the lid piece. Sew it down at both ends and in the center to create two loops.
4.  **Join lid to body:** Take a larger, lined fabric rectangle. Align the non-zippered edge of the lid piece with one short edge of the large rectangle, right sides together. Sew them together to create a hinge. Trim any uneven edges.
5.  **Form a tube:** Bring the opposite short edge of the large rectangle around to meet the free side of the zipper. Ensure the lining side of the large rectangle is facing outwards. Sew the zipper to this edge.
6.  **Close the ends:** Flatten the fabric tube so the zipper is centered. Insert small, folded fabric pull tabs inside each end of the zipper, sandwiched between the layers. Sew straight across the two open ends of the tube to close them.
7.  **Box the corners:** At each of the four corners, pinch the fabric flat so the end seam aligns with the folded edge of the tube, creating a point. Sew a straight line across the base of the resulting triangle. Cut off the excess fabric tip.
8.  **Finish:** Unzip the bag and turn the entire project right-side out to reveal the finished exterior.

tips.title: Boxed corners with lining seams still connected
tips.notes: FB yt-dlp cookies+subs batch 1 (2026-09-08): non-EN auto-captions (es/id/pt) → EN transcript in scrapes/06e63b4053/dl/transcript.txt; how_to from spoken construction steps.
tips.how_to:
1. When sewing a lined pouch/bag, sew side seams but start/stop at each end of the lining opening so corner seams stay connected (no need to cut threads).
2. For each layer, separate the fabric, pull the sides, and match the seam edges; connected seams make centering easier.
3. Press seams open and flatten the sides; repeat on the lining, stack evenly, and clip.
4. Stitch across through all layers to form the boxed corner, backtacking at both ends.
5. Alternate method: nest seams instead of pressing open—lower seam facing down, lining nested opposite—so the presser foot does not catch; open-seam side lies flat, nested side has a small lip.
6. Repeat on remaining corners so lining stays locked in place.

tips.title: Small boxy zipper pouch (16×28 cm panels)

2. Outer face-up; zipper face-down on a 16cm edge; lining face-down on top (zipper sandwiched). Sew that edge.

tips.how_to: Press the strip like double-fold bias/strap (raw long edges toward center, then fold). At each short end, fold the two corners diagonally into the center crease so raw ends are enclosed (house/pointed tip). Topstitch both long edges and across the finished ends. Clean straps, tabs, or ties without a tube-turn.

tips.title: Perfect right-angle fabric corners (fold & stitch)
tips.notes: Creator: @sheryart61. Scrape: scrapes/bce87fb21d/
tips.how_to: To turn a clean right-angle corner quickly: fold the piece so the raw edges that form the corner meet, mark a straight stitch line across the fold where the corner should sit, and sew that straight line. Trim the excess triangle, then turn the corner out and poke/press for a sharp right angle. Sewing a straight line on the fold is easier than trying to pivot a perfect 90° while turning.

tips.title: Zipper pocket in tote bag lining
tips.notes: Creator: @jennsews. Full ~4.5 min tutorial. Scrape: scrapes/817ddb885a/
tips.how_to: Cut a pocket rectangle with fusible interfacing on the back (example: 9″ × 14″ for a ~7″ zipper opening with ~1″ margins). On the interfacing side, mark the zipper window (e.g. 1.5″ down from top), stitch the window rectangle, slash center and clip corners, then turn and press. Sew the zipper behind the window. Fold the pocket fabric up to form the pocket bag, stitch sides/bottom, and attach this unit to the lining panel before assembling the bag lining.

tips.title: Boxed-corner bag bottom (extratotes sewing tip)
tips.notes: Creator: @extratotes. Silent 60s technique clip—boxed corners on mauve linen-like tote. Scrape: scrapes/e14062b757/
tips.how_to: After sewing the pouch/bag body (sides + bottom), turn so a side seam and bottom fold meet. Pinch the corner, flatten into a triangle with the side seam centered on the triangle, and measure the desired depth across the triangle base. Stitch straight across that line; trim the excess triangle. Repeat on the other corner. Turn RS out for a flat, boxy bottom. Optional: fold/clip a top hem or casing and topstitch before or after boxing.

Turn the strap right-side out once (or twice as needed for the fold structure), poke the corner square with a point turner, and press. Topstitch both long edges. Works for tote straps, lanyards, and narrow straps that are hard to turn when sewn as a tube.

Build a rectangular gusset strip: fold fabric over a zipper (or sew zipper into the strip center) so the zip opens along the side wall. Sew the zip gusset around one circle (clip curves), then attach the other circle, leaving the zipper open enough to turn. Finish raw edges or bind if needed. Sew front crotch rise RST; sew back crotch rise RST; join front to back at side seams; sew inseam aligning rises and any borders. Finish SA (zigzag if no serger—terry sheds). Fold a waist channel for your elastic (example: 1″ elastic → ~1½″ fold), sew leaving a gap, thread elastic with safety pins, try on, overlap and box-stitch elastic, close gap.

tips.title: Double ruffle elastic strap
tips.notes: Creator: @sewingjulie. Scrape: scrapes/2600e3346f/
tips.how_to: Cut two fabric strips, one slightly wider than the other. Layer them right sides up (wider underneath or as desired), pin so layers do not shift, and mark the center line of the stack. Place elastic (finished strap length) along that center line and sew a few cm to anchor. Then stretch the elastic fully while sewing a straight seam down the center. When released, both layers gather into a double ruffle that is stretchy enough for dress straps.

tips.title: Boxy-corner tote with two external slip pockets
tips.notes: Uploader: backstitch.company. One-part beginner tutorial; screenshot pattern mockup in video.
tips.how_to: Cut three matching body panels (front, back, bottom) plus linings; optional thrifted blanket as batting. Quilt or mark lines if desired. Build each external pocket: fold a long pocket rectangle in half, bind/fold a narrow edge strip (~2″ folded to ~½″), sandwich the pocket edge, and sew the pocket to the front/back body; add vertical stitch lines to divide compartments. Double-fold straps (example: 6″ width folded down to ~1½″) and stitch. Sew the bottom panel RST to front and back to join the three body pieces, sew the side seams, and box the corners. Sew the lining as a box with boxed corners, leaving a gap to turn. Nest outer into lining RST with straps tucked inside between layers; sew the top edge. Turn through the lining gap, poke corners, press, and topstitch the top edge.

tips.title: Zipper tabs + sandwich insert for a clean zipper bag
tips.notes: Creator: @sweetcinnamonroses. Reply to comment about messy zipper borders. Scrape: scrapes/8c077ae067/
tips.how_to: Add fabric zipper tabs to both zipper ends (fold small rectangles over trimmed zipper tape; stitch across) so side seams don’t chew zipper stops. Sandwich zipper between outer and lining (or quilted panel + lining) RST; stitch with zipper foot; flip and press. Repeat for the other panel. Then place quilted panel against quilted panel (RST), sew sides/bottom, turn. Tabs give a clean border finish at the zipper ends. Short reply video—full version on long-form.

tips.title: Reversible bible/book cover with fabric ties (drawstring-style)
tips.notes: Creator: @sewwithcesia / Cesia Mendoza. On-screen: measure +3″; batting as WS; ½″ SA; double-pin stop; turn via gap; ties through side opening. Scrape: scrapes/45f3dbd70a/
tips.how_to: Measure book width and length; add 3″ to each (ex: 6×9 book → cut 9×12). Cut 2 mains (outer + reverse), 2 batting same size. Treat batting as the wrong side of each main: layer batting behind each main, place mains RST, sew ½″ SA around, leaving a turning gap (double-clip/pin to mark where to stop). Trim SA/corners; turn RS out through the gap; press. Topstitch opening closed. Make long fabric ties (fold/press strip, stitch); leave or create a small side-seam opening near the open edge and thread ties through so the cover cinches closed. Beginner-friendly reversible cozy.

tips.title: Bow-strap boxed tote (thrifted sheets)
tips.notes: Uploader: lauren.lieser19. Beginner boxed tote with statement bow straps.
tips.how_to: Cut two outer and two lining body pieces (on-screen sizes). Cut 3″×3″ squares from both bottom corners of all four pieces. Sew outer RST on sides + bottom (not across cut squares); box corners by matching side seam to bottom seam and sewing straight; repeat for lining. Cut four strap pieces; sew pairs RST with angled ends, leave bottom open, clip points, turn, press—these become bow-like straps. Outer right-side out inside lining wrong-side out (RST); sandwich straps at side seams between layers; sew top leaving a gap; turn; topstitch to close gap and lock lining.

tips.title: Beginner double-fold gathered ruffle (math + two basting rows)
tips.notes: Uploader: curious.handmade. Maker mentions a downloadable PDF calculator.
tips.how_to: Measure the edge to cover (e.g. tote sides + bottom). Width of strip = measured length + ¼″ SA at each end, then ×1.5 for a loose ruffle or ×2 for a tighter ruffle. Depth = desired finished depth ×2 + SA. Cut, press, fold RST lengthwise; sew both short ends ¼″; clip corners; turn and press. Set longest stitch; leave long tails; sew two gathering rows just inside the SA (~¼″ and ~⅛″ from the raw long edge). Pull bobbin threads gently from both ends until the ruffle matches the target length; distribute gathers evenly. Attach to the project with the gathered raw edge in the seam.

tips.title: Terry-cloth pool / swim-team pants from beach towels
tips.notes: Creator: @sewcutebykatie. Scrape: scrapes/e5d2630dd8/
tips.how_to: Draft from RTW pajama pants: turn them inside out, tuck one leg into the other, and use as a pattern. Cut each leg from a beach towel (or two coordinating towels), placing the hem along the towel’s finished edge so you skip hemming; cut ~1″ wider than the pajama for ease and ~2″ taller at the waist for an elastic casing. Serge/zigzag raw edges so terry doesn’t fray. Sew each leg’s side seam RST, then join the crotch seams matching the inseams. Optional: add a contrast side pocket from the opposite towel. Fold the waist down into a casing, topstitch, leave a back opening; feed elastic with a bodkin or safety pin, sew elastic ends, and close the opening.

tips.title: Sew photos/paper into a banner (machines aren’t just for fabric)
tips.notes: Creator: @jessmakesclothes. Short visual tip. Scrape: scrapes/6e6fe711a3/
tips.how_to: Use a sewing machine to stitch through printed photographs or heavy paper/cardstock to join them into a banner or mixed-media strip. Guide slowly under the presser foot with regular thread (pink shown). Tip: sewing paper dulls needles faster—use a dedicated needle or swap after. tips.title: Spring Roll Pouch sew-along (Love You Sew pattern / Sew Hungry Hippie)
tips.notes: Creator: Sew Hungry Hippie. Pattern: Love You Sew. ~1h46m membership sew-along. Scrape: scrapes/1b9518381a/
tips.how_to: Follow the Love You Sew Spring Roll Pouch pattern (subscription box sew-along with Natalie @ Sew Hungry Hippie). Rough workflow from the video: cut main body and optional divider/slip/elastic pockets per pattern; cut foam (non-fusible preferred) oversized and baste to outers; fuse woven interfacing (e.g. SF101) to handle and needed linings. Make double-fold handle, tack short ends under, baste to back of main body. Add zipper tabs (fold like “Pac-Man,” insert zipper to fold, stitch across nylon teeth OK). Build divider zip pocket by sandwiching zipper between pieces, zipper-foot sew, topstitch seam allowances away from teeth; repeat other side. Match exteriors/interiors RST, push zipper toward interior, sew sides stopping at marked dots before zipper tabs (slightly different SA exterior vs lining). Turn via zipper; continue pattern steps for remaining pockets/assembly. Video is a guide—read the printed pattern; optional pockets can be skipped.

tips.title: Big bag with zipper pocket inside
Quilted boxy zipper makeup pouch (AmyG DIY)
tips.notes: Creator: AmyG DIY (@AmyGDIY). YT had no captions; steps from video frames (fabric+batting overlay, zipper sandwich, boxed corners). Scrape: scrapes/7e7191194a/
tips.how_to: Layer outer fabric + cotton batting (and optional second fabric); pin and quilt with parallel channels (~½–1″ apart). Cut quilted panels as rectangles with square notches at the corners for boxing. Sandwich zipper between quilted outer and lining (or batting/lining): RST/zip face-down along the long edge, stitch with zipper foot (snips/stiletto help feed bulky layers), flip and topstitch; repeat other side so zipper sits between two panels. Sew sides and notch edges; box corners; turn RS out. Optional ribbon loop at zipper end as pull/tab. Finished: quilted rectangular box pouch with centered zipper.

tips.title: Lay-flat collapsible travel shoe bag (Hello Sewing)
tips.notes: Creator: Hello Sewing (hellosewing.com/shoe-bag-pattern/). YT had no captions; steps from matching free tutorial. Scrape: scrapes/d275fd3551/
tips.how_to: Cut: outer 24″×15″, lining 24″×15″, handle 3¼″×8¾″, two binding strips 1½″×8″; 15″ (or 40 cm) plastic zipper. Finished ~6¾″×14″ (fits ~EU43/US9.5; enlarge fabric for bigger shoes). Split zipper into two tapes. Sandwich each zipper half between outer+lining short edges; sew with zipper foot; turn; press; topstitch. Fold so zipper sides meet; mark centers. Reinstall zipper pull; bring zipper ends to center marks (lining out). Mark 2″ in from side folds for expansion pleats. Make double-fold handle; stitch; pin ends at top center. Fold sides in on the 2″ lines; sew top & bottom ¼″ catching handle. Bind raw ends with the 1½″ strips (sew, wrap, stitch). Turn RS out through zipper.

tips.title: Easy boxy zipper pouch for beginners
tips.notes: Creator: @baylin.diy. Scrape: scrapes/7700312254/
tips.how_to: Place fabric pieces RST and sew a short seam (~2 cm from the edge) where the zipper will sit, then center the zipper on that seam and stitch around to install it. Sew the remaining end of the pouch closed. Flip right-side out, then box the corners by flattening each bottom corner into a triangle, marking the desired depth, sewing across, and trimming excess. Simple beginner boxy pouch construction.

tips.title: Quilted envelope jewelry / tea pouch with clasp
tips.notes: Creator: @withbreck. Scrape: scrapes/1741e3ef7d/
tips.how_to: Trace an existing small pouch (or draw two rectangles with a triangle flap) for an envelope shape. Cut 2 fashion fabric + 1 cotton batting. Layer fabric on batting, then fabric RST; sew around leaving an opening; turn RS out; quilt decorative lines; stitch opening closed. Install a clasp kit (or Velcro) on the flap. Fold the square up and sew the side seams (add a tag if desired). Good for jewelry or loose-leaf tea travel.

tips.title: No-pattern boxy toiletry bag with handle (from one rectangle)
tips.notes: Uploader: guruandboone. Single-piece construction; serge tip in caption.
tips.how_to: Cut one fabric rectangle 16″×12″. Sew zipper face-down to one long edge; fold fabric RST and sew the other zipper side; topstitch both sides of the zipper. Press so the zipper sits centered on a flat rectangle. Open zipper halfway; sew both short ends closed. Box all four corners by pinching side to bottom; measure ~1¾″ in and sew. On the handle corners, leave a small opening in the boxed seam, insert one handle end, then sew closed; turn and insert the other handle end the same way. Optional: serge interior seams for a cleaner look (not structurally required).

tips.title: Ruffle makeup bag — part 1 (quilt, ruffle, zipper attach)
tips.notes: Uploader: ehaskell_. Part 1 only; pair with part 2 when linked.
tips.how_to: Template ~8½″×11″ (letter paper). Cut 2 outer, 2 lining; cut ruffle strips, zipper (prefer longer than 11″), and zipper tabs (on-screen measurements). Optionally tack the zipper stop end. Fold ruffle WST to ~1½″ finished width. Gather with longest stitch + high tension while holding the spool/thread path for controlled gathers. Quilt outers to fusible fleece (e.g. 1½″ grid). Pin ruffle along top of outer, zipper teeth-down on top; sew close to teeth; then sew lining RST over same seam. Flip lining to wrong side against fleece, topstitch ruffle/zipper. Repeat for the other side, keeping 8½″ edges aligned. Part 2 finishes assembly (see related tip / maker’s page).

tips.title: Tapered flat zipper makeup bag (11″ paper pattern)
tips.notes: Uploader: halle_ellis. Pattern drafting in caption: 11″ square with 2.5″ bottom insets.
tips.how_to: Draft: start with an 11″ paper square; on the bottom edge mark 2.5″ in from each side; connect those dots to the top corners to make a tapered shape (caption pattern). Quilt outer to batting and cut two outers + two linings from the shape; zipper at least as long as the top (~11″). Sandwich zipper between outer and lining; sew; topstitch; repeat for the other side. Open zipper; pin outer corners together and lining corners together; sew around leaving a lining turning gap. Match side/bottom seams at each corner, mark 2″ from the tip, sew across, trim the triangle. Turn, poke corners, and close the lining gap.

tips.title: Quilted Kindle sleeve with ribbon ties (8×6 cuts)
tips.notes: Creator: @sendit2merachel. On-screen cut list and steps: RST leave one short side open; ribbons mid-sides; flip out. Scrape: scrapes/a6fe907f91/
tips.how_to: Cut: (2) batting 8×6, (2) lining 8×6, (2) outer 8×6, (2) ribbon 8×2.5. Quilt/baste each outer to batting. Place the two quilted outers RST; sew around leaving one short side open. Make ribbon ties (fold/press 8×2.5 strips). Place lining pieces RST with outers as needed, insert one ribbon centered on each long side, sew, then flip out through the open short end; close opening and topstitch. Flat quilted sleeve that protects the Kindle from scratches.

tips.title: Upgrade bag handles with folded webbing grip
tips.notes: FB yt-dlp cookies+subs batch 1 (2026-09-08): auto-captions → scrapes/a0c151f162/dl/transcript.txt; how_to from spoken steps.
tips.how_to:
1. Use premade webbing with the right side facing you; fold in half to mark the center.
2. From the center, mark 3½ in to each side (about 7 in total grip zone).
3. Starting at one outer mark, fold the webbing in half lengthwise and clip to the other mark so the folded edge will face outside the bag and the cut edges face inward.
4. Stitch about ⅛ in from each long edge between the start and end marks, backstitching at both ends; repeat on the folded-over side.
5. Match thread to the webbing so stitches blend; remove marking lines (heat-erasable pen + iron after testing on a scrap).
6. Attach the finished handles to your bag as usual.

tips.title: Large quilted boxy pouch (no bias tape)
tips.notes: Uploader: mariahs_makes. Clean finish without bias binding.
tips.how_to: Fuse outer to fusible fleece; quilt (e.g. diagonal lines with a 1½″ guide); trim quilted outers to 14″×11″. Make double-fold zipper pull tabs and stitch.
